title: Sphere packing in dimensions 8, 24 and 3: an independent check of the formal proofs

contributors.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
contributors.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
The Lean 4 and Mathlib proofs that E₈ gives the densest sphere packing in dimension 8 (density π⁴/384, Viazovska) and the Leech lattice the densest in dimension 24 (density π¹²/12!, Cohn, Kumar, Miller, Radchenko and Viazovska), with the uniqueness of the Leech packing among periodic packings. The Lean development is copied unchanged from math-inc/Sphere-Packing-Lean at commit 1e98fb4 (Apache-2.0). It was begun at EPFL by Sidharth Hariharan and Maryna Viazovska with Birkbeck, Lee, Ma, Mehta and Poiroux (arXiv:2604.23468) and completed in dimensions 8 and 24 by Math, Inc.'s autoformalization agent Gauss; they are the creators of this record.

The archive adds an independent check: a static scan of all 180,649 lines finding no sorry, axiom, native_decide or other kernel bypass; an audit of the definitions behind the headline statements, which concern the supremum of the upper density over all packings, not only lattice or periodic ones; a CI build with #print axioms of every headline theorem and a leanchecker replay of all 829 SpherePacking modules; and Python, Julia, C and C++ checks that the lattices in the Lean source are E₈ and the Leech lattice (even unimodular, 240 and 0 roots, 2160 and 196560 vectors of norm 4, the two densities). It also records that no complete Lean proof of the Kepler conjecture exists; Flyspeck, in HOL Light and Isabelle, is the only complete formal proof in dimension 3.
notes: The formal proofs are the work of the creators listed (math-inc/Sphere-Packing-Lean, Apache-2.0, sphere-packing/LICENSE). The checks in verification/, VERIFICATION.md and kepler/STATUS.md were added by Deep Bhattacharjee (d.bhattacharjee@erl-forschung.de; itsdeep@live.com) under the MIT licence in LICENSE.
